summary: W75 joins loaded PE TLS indices to the current process threads and matches live static TLS vectors and module data blocks to real default-heap entries. The Win64 TEB profile is validated against the calling thread and the independently linked executable anchor. Loader membership, indices, thread lifetime and vector pointers are checked around the walk. Two consistent null-vector observations account for live Windows helper threads without static TLS. A controlled Release DLL verifies isolated cells for the main thread and two workers created on opposite sides of the load. The exact worker heap blocks disappear after join and the DLL leaves the module table after unload. Flat and Full account for every observed process thread across four native checkpoints. All 46 Release regression groups and seven related cases pass.

scope: Windows Release static TLS vector and loaded-module heap payload and overhead at native lifecycle phases
composition_rule: One actual confirmed heap allocation contributes once. Module and thread rollups describe the same module blocks. The vector and module storage are distinct allocations. Executable TLS overlaps previously observed W57 blocks. The active blocks are a subset of process heap memory. Retained replaced vectors and dynamic TLS/FLS lie outside this measurement.
